expectations.evidence: References Biome, Vitest, Drizzle ORM, gramjs/telegram, pino, Zod, Claude API, Vite, Tailwind CSS, ESLint, Framer Motion, lucide-react by name. Includes pipeline-specific module boundary table and build commands.
All rules are TypeScript/Node.js specific. No Python rules present.

Section 4 'Test Anti-Patterns (Reject These)' lists: (a) tests that only assert toBeDefined() or not.toBeNull(), (b) tests that duplicate implementation logic, (c) snapshot tests for business logic, (d) vague test names addressed via naming convention requirement, (e) mocking the function under test itself. All 5 of 5 addressed.
Backcom without_skill output is 343 lines with 15 sections. This is larger than the minimal project without_skill (215 lines, 11 sections), which is the correct proportional relationship.

Section 11 'Safety Rules -- NEVER Violate' covers Telegram-specific rules (rate limits, reply delay jitter 45-180s), forex compliance (no profit claims, no broker names, NFA disclaimer, no urgency language), and content safety. Section 15 covers pipeline architecture and phase discipline.
No section asks the user where to place the rules. The output is presented as a standalone document without any placement options or questions.

The output does not acknowledge the existing CLAUDE.md. It presents rules as if from scratch, including sections (naming conventions, module boundaries, build commands, Result<T,E> pattern) that are already in the existing CLAUDE.md, leading to wholesale duplication.
